title: Count only 'Depends on' ids and retry links as plan dependencies
summary: The plan builds each item's dependencies from every job id quoted anywhere in the request text, so a request that cites a rejected job as evidence is held forever. Change it so only ids on a 'Depends on' line, or the retry link of a "try again on" request, are dependencies; the people waiting on the 29 held items are the audience.

defaults_applied.how: New tests for the planned and held cases; fmt, clippy -D warnings and cargo test must pass.
Criterion checks athena plan on this queue holds no item for ids outside 'Depends on' lines.
Fix the dependency extraction in plan_entry, not the hold step.
Criteria run tests that show items planned or held.
One focused change to dependency extraction plus tests and changelog.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs: plan_entry (about line 2125) sets entry.depends_on from job_ids_in(text), every job id anywhere in the request; this is the root cause. crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs: Plan::build_with holds an item when a depends_on id is rejected or failed with no landed retry (unmet_dependency, retries); crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs entry_of calls plan_entry, which is the entry point for athena plan. Order: dependencies are extracted in plan_entry, then held or ordered in build_with.

The request names plan.rs, but the dependency extraction lives in reading.rs plan_entry, so reading.rs is listed as a deliverable too; plan.rs is changed only if its docs or tests need it. Held-reason and retry logic in plan.rs stay as they are.

A 'Depends on' line is a line whose text starts with 'Depends on' (case-insensitive, optional leading '>' or list marker), and every full job id on it is a dependency. A 'try again on <id>' request keeps that id as its retry link and dependency.

The old 'after <job>' and follow-up phrase handling does not make dependencies; ids there are references. The existing 'referenced job not among the records' open question may still cover all quoted ids, since it is a reference check.
No new record or data file is added, so the records allow-list is untouched. The change adds no refusal rule to readings; it releases held items, so no refusal-rate figure applies.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test through Plan::build_with (with a plan_entry built from request text) shows a request that quotes a rejected job id in its text with no 'Depends on' line is planned, not in Plan::refused. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.

A new test shows a request with a 'Depends on <id>' line naming a rejected job with no landed retry is still held, and its Refusal reason contains 'depends on <id>' and 'rejected'. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.

A new test shows a 'try again on <id>' request still depends on that id, and that an id in a 'Depends on' line is a dependency while the same id elsewhere in the text is not. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
Run on this repository's queue, athena plan (cargo run -- plan) holds no item whose only rejected or failed id is outside a 'Depends on' line; the job report shows this.
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test all pass, including the existing reading test about job ids at reading.rs around line 4164, updated to the new rule.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry that says only 'Depends on' ids and retry links are dependencies and that cited job ids no longer hold an item.
The doc comment of plan_entry in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs states the new rule in place of 'depends on every other job whose full id it names'.

out_of_scope: Changing how rejected or failed dependencies are held, or the held reason text
Releasing or re-reading the held items by hand
Changing athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflow files
Changing the 'referenced job not among the records' open question beyond what the new rule needs
departures: The extraction is in reading.rs rather than the named plan.rs, a small risk of verifier mismatch with the stated Files line.
urgent_reason: Removes the permanent holding of 29 queued items, including urgent fixes, which is wasted time and blocked planning.
hard_reason: It changes the rule that decides which items the plan holds back, so a mistake would hide or wrongly release queued work.
